'''Raymond Bernard Felton Jr.''' (born [[June 26]], [[1984]] in [[Latta, South Carolina]]) is a point guard for the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill#Athletics|Tar Heels]]. At 6'1", 198 pounds, he is one of college basketball's best guards. At high school, Raymond was named [[National High School Player of the Year]] in 2002, led his high school to two state championships and a high school career record of 104-9.  He was named to the All-American Team and he set 2 South Carolina state records.  In his freshman year, he was voted Carolina Player of the Year and ACC [[Freshman]] of the Week three times.  He had 236 assists, and averaged 12.0 points a game.  In his sophmore year, he was a finalist for the Bob Cousy Award and the Naismith Award, and had 213 assists.  Raymond led the Tar Heels in steals (63) and free throw percentage (81%).  Not only this, but he averaged 11.5 points per game. In his third and final season Carolina, Raymond lead his school, along with fellow juniors [[Rashad McCants]] and [[Sean May]], to the 2005 National Championship over the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] [[Fighting Illini]] on April 4, 2005 in [[St. Louis]], the 4th Title in UNC's history. While averaging 12.9 points and 6.9 assists per game, Felton improved his shooting very much in his junior season and is considered a Top 10 pick in the 2005 [[NBA Draft]].
